strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH-63278 (PR 63509): Period construction from a near-minimum microsecond Timestamp overflows int64 in npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime / scaleSecondsToMicroseconds on the buggy commit 73e3149d1311. Build pandas from source at the buggy revision with the PR's test file applied, then run the single new test. It should error with OverflowError on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed revision.

pinned_because: No Python version is stated by the evidence, so none is pinned; use a Python version the buggy revision's pyproject.toml supports.

NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented or era-derived constraint in the context. NumPy>=2.0 and Cython>=3.0 are my choices, not evidence-derived. NumPy is numerically relevant only through the C datetime code, which is compiled into pandas.
Build-system packages (meson-python, meson, versioneer) are taken from the project's build requirements as the usual pandas source build; the context does not state them.
tzdata is needed only on Windows/Emscripten per the README, so it is not required on Linux but is harmless to install.
git tags are needed so versioneer can compute a version when building from a checkout.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/period/test_period.py::TestPeriodConstruction::test_construction_from_min_timestamp (added by the PR diff; the enclosing class name is inferred from the diff location and may differ)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 73e3149d1311 the test errors: Period(ts, freq='us') raises OverflowError from np_datetime.c before any field assertion runs, so the test fails. On the fixed revision the Period constructs and the six assertions comparing per.year, month, day, hour, minute and second to ts's fields all hold, so the test passes. The transition is fail to pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Construct ts = Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='us') and then Period(ts, freq='us'). The buggy build raises OverflowError; the fixed build returns a Period. Only the exception-versus-success outcome matters for the transition.

input_output_examples.input: ts = pd.Timestamp(pd.Timestamp.min.value, unit="us"); per = pd.Period(ts, freq="us")
input_output_examples.buggy_output: OverflowError: Overflow occurred at ../../pandas/_libs/src/vendored/numpy/datetime/np_datetime.c:458; the reporter also saw per display as Period('1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000', 'us')
input_output_examples.expected_output: A valid Period whose year, month, day, hour, minute and second equal those of ts (exact numeric values not given in the evidence)

risks: The bug is an int64 overflow in signed C arithmetic. Under -fsanitize=undefined or other sanitizer builds it may trap at a different point, so the buggy revision may not reproduce the same exception text. Use a plain optimised build like the one the project ships.

Whether the wrapped value reaches the Python layer depends on compiler optimisation of signed overflow. The reporter's 1970-01-01 result suggests wrap-around, but that is observed behaviour, not a guaranteed one; the failure may show as an exception on some compilers and as wrong fields on others. The test asserts on fields, so either outcome should still fail on the buggy revision.

The 'exception ignored in get_period_ordinal' message suggests the overflow check is raised from a Cython callback. Confirm the buggy build has PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW active; a build with overflow checks disabled would give silent wrong values and could fail the assertions for different reasons.
The round-trip to_timestamp check is commented out because the result is out of nanosecond bounds, so it cannot be used as an oracle. The test relies only on the field comparisons against ts.
The reproduction depends on the test file from the PR being applied on top of the buggy revision. Without that test, no transition can be observed.

Only x86-64 Linux is implied by the evidence. The reporter's platform is not stated, and platform-specific behaviour is not established. If the defect only appears on a particular architecture or toolchain, the test will not transition elsewhere.

oracle.reference_source: The expected field values come from ts itself (ts.year, ts.month, ts.day, ts.hour, ts.minute, ts.second), not from the buggy output.
oracle.why: The test compares integer calendar fields, so an exact comparison is appropriate. The buggy output 1970-01-01 is wrong and must not be used as the expected value.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Period(ts, freq='us') raises OverflowError inside get_period_ordinal, so the test errors before reaching any assertion. The overflow comes from seconds * 10**6 for seconds near -9223372036855 wrapping in int64.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed revision splits the scaled value into two checked parts, so Period constructs without overflow and the six field assertions match ts's fields.
